fixture.label: Brand Glossary of the fictional brand Aamod.

review_status: Drafted by the demo author. Spellings and language notes should be confirmed by native-speaker reviewers before any real use.
rules: Logos and the pack always keep the Latin wordmark; the spellings below are for running text in other scripts.
Use these spellings exactly. If a script has no entry, request a review instead of improvising one.
Regional terms marked translate = "adapt" belong to their region: replace them with that region's own term, backed by evidence, instead of translating them.

pronunciation.guide: AA-mode: a long 'aa' as in 'father', a long 'o' as in 'go', and a soft dental 'd' (tongue against the teeth). Stress is light and even.

language_notes.mr: आमोद means delight or joy; also fragrance.
language_notes.bn: আমোদ means fun, amusement. Bengali speakers will say 'Amod'; that is acceptable.
language_notes.ta: Close to ஆமோதம் (approval, assent), a neutral word. The final த் is said as a soft 'd'.

language_notes.all: Transliterate only; never replace 'Festive Tin' with a local word for box or tin.
language_notes.mr: फेस्टिव्ह follows Marathi spelling of English 'v' at the end of a word; Hindi copy would use फेस्टिव.

language_notes.all: Shown and voiced in English in every region. A local-language line may precede it, never replace it.

language_notes.mr: The Diwali assortment of homemade snacks and sweets: chakli, karanji, besan ladoo, shankarpali, chivda.
language_notes.all: Maharashtra-specific. Do not carry the word or the item list into other states; find each region's own festive term and items through Market Lens evidence.

language_notes.mr: The sibling day after Diwali: the sister performs aukshan (aarti) for her brother, who gives her a gift.
language_notes.all: Marathi name. Check each region's own name, date and importance for this day before using it in copy or in a delivery promise.

language_notes.mr: The paper lantern hung outside homes at Diwali.
language_notes.all: A Maharashtra Diwali visual; check the target region's own festive decoration.
Standard greetings, to be confirmed by native reviewers. Whether a Diwali greeting is the right festive greeting at all in a region is a Market Lens question, not a translation question.
